classification.difficultyReason: Combine two half-planes, distinguish included and excluded boundaries, and calculate each boundary intersection.

content.prompt: Sketch each region and find the coordinates of the corner points.

answer.short: Corner point: $(4,-3)$, excluded. Shade to the right of $x=4$ and on or below $y=-3$.
answer.worked: The boundaries intersect at $(4,-3)$. Draw $x=4$ dashed because $x>4$, and $y=-3$ solid because $y\le -3$. Shade their common region to the right of the vertical line and below the horizontal line. Mark the corner with an open circle because $x=4$ is excluded.

spec.description: Common region right of a dashed vertical boundary and below a solid horizontal boundary, with an open corner.
spec.mathematics: x>4 and y<=-3; boundary intersection (4,-3) is excluded.

answer.short: Corner point: $(6,12)$, included. Shade on or below $y=2x$ and on or left of $x=6$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x&=6\\y&=2(6)\\y&=12\end{align*}$$
Draw both boundaries solid. Shade below $y=2x$ and left of $x=6$. Their common region has the included corner $(6,12)$.

spec.description: Solid boundaries y=2x and x=6, with their common lower-left region shaded.
spec.mathematics: Boundary intersection (6,12) belongs to both non-strict inequalities.

answer.short: Corner point: $\left(\frac43,\frac83\right)$, included. Shade on or below both lines.
answer.worked:
At the intersection, $y=2x$ and $x+y=4$.
$$\begin{align*}x+2x&=4\\3x&=4\\x&=\frac43\\y&=2\left(\frac43\right)\\y&=\frac83\end{align*}$$
Draw both boundaries solid and shade their common region below both lines. The corner $\left(\frac43,\frac83\right)$ is included.

spec.description: Solid intersecting boundaries with the common region below both lines shaded.

answer.short: Corner point: $\left(-\frac13,\frac53\right)$, excluded. Shade above $y=x+2$ and on or below $y=1-2x$, to the left of their intersection.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}1-2x&=x+2\\-3x&=1\\x&=-\frac13\\y&=-\frac13+2\\y&=\frac53\end{align*}$$
Draw $y=1-2x$ solid and $y=x+2$ dashed. Shade the common region between them to the left of the intersection. Mark $\left(-\frac13,\frac53\right)$ open because it lies on the excluded boundary $y=x+2$.

spec.description: Region between the solid descending line and dashed ascending line, extending left from an open corner.

answer.short: Corner point: $(2,2)$, included. Shade on or above $y=4-x$ and on or below $y=6-2x$.
answer.worked:
At the intersection, $y=4-x$.
$$\begin{align*}2x+(4-x)&=6\\x+4&=6\\x&=2\\y&=4-2\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Draw both boundaries solid. Shade between the lines to the left of the included corner $(2,2)$.

spec.description: Two solid descending boundaries enclosing a shaded wedge extending left from (2,2).

answer.short: Corner point: $(-3,9)$, included. Shade on or above $y=-2x+3$ and on or below $y=6-x$.
answer.worked:
At the intersection, $y=-2x+3$.
$$\begin{align*}x+(-2x+3)&=6\\-x+3&=6\\x&=-3\\y&=-2(-3)+3\\y&=9\end{align*}$$
Draw both boundaries solid. Shade between the lines to the right of the included corner $(-3,9)$.

spec.description: Two solid descending boundaries enclosing the common shaded wedge extending right from (-3,9).
